2027-01-21.title: Third Thursday of Denha · Thursday after the Three Days' Fast
2027-01-21.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked
Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity?
No greater joy than to hear that my children walk in the truth
Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents
2027-01-21.alt: Season of Denha. Thanksgiving after the Three Days' Fast. Church Unity Octave.
2027-01-21.verse: Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
theo: The fast is over, and the Church celebrates the joy of God who forgives. Ezekiel hears God swear: “As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live.” Micah sings: “Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity…? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency… You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.” After three days of turning, we hear God's answer: mercy.

In the Gospel tax collectors and sinners come near to Jesus, and the Pharisees grumble. Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one lost sheep, and of a woman who sweeps her house to find one lost coin. When they find them, they call their neighbours: “Rejoice with me.” “Just so… there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.” John the Elder writes: “I have no greater joy than this, to hear that my children are walking in the truth.” The fruit of the fast is joy: God's joy over us, and our joy in walking in his truth.
outline: Ask: have you ever found something precious you had lost?
Micah's God who delights in mercy.
“Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.”
live: Thank God tonight for the graces of the three days.
Contact one person who has drifted from you or from the Church.
2027-01-21.prayer: God of mercy, you take no pleasure in the death of sinners and you cast our sins into the depths of the sea. Thank you for the grace of these days of fasting. Let us share heaven's joy over every sinner who returns, and walk always in your truth. Amen.
altar: Each Qurbana is a feast of the found: we were lost, and the Shepherd carries us home on his shoulders to his table.

2027-01-21.question: Do I share God's joy when a sinner returns, or do I grumble?

family.explain: A shepherd lost one sheep. He looked everywhere until he found it, then carried it home happily. God is that happy when someone comes back to him!
family.intention: We pray for people who are lost and far from God.
family.ask: Ask: “How did the fast help our family?”

illus: In Kerala fishing villages, when a boat lost at sea for days finally returns, the whole beach runs to meet it, church bells ring and there is a feast. A fisherman said: that is how heaven is when one of us comes back to God.

pm.open: God of mercy, the fast is over and your mercy remains. Fill us with your joy over every sinner who returns. Amen.
share: I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked (Ezekiel 33:11). Do I believe God wants me to live?
You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea (Micah 7:19). What sin do I need to leave there?
Rejoice with me (Luke 15:6). Do I rejoice when others return to God?
pm.resp: Lord, we rejoice in your mercy.
interc: In thanksgiving for the graces of the Three Days' Fast.
For those still far from God.
For priests who seek the lost.
For families waiting for a member to return.
pm.close: Father, you delight in showing mercy. Keep us in the joy of your forgiveness and make us seekers of the lost. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the Three Days' Fast is over, and today the Church celebrates God's joy. Through Ezekiel God swears: as I live, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live (Ezekiel 33:11).

Micah sings: who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity? He delights in showing clemency. You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea (Micah 7:18–19). What we brought to God in these three days, he has thrown into the sea.

In the Gospel Jesus tells of a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to find one, and of a woman who searches her whole house for one coin. When they find them they say: rejoice with me. Just so, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:6–7).
John the Elder writes: I have no greater joy than this, to hear that my children are walking in the truth (3 John 4). Let the fruit of our fast be joy, and let us become seekers of the lost. Amen.
kids: Children, a shepherd found his lost sheep and was so happy! God is that happy when we come back to him. Thank God for these three days of fasting.

intro: Theme: “Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.”
After the fast: the God who delights in mercy, and the joy of the found.

q: Say to them, As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live; turn back, turn back from your evil ways; for why will you die, O house of Israel?
The Lord is not slow about his promise, as some think of slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.
points.apply: Thank God for his patience with you.

q: He will again have compassion upon us; he will tread our iniquities under foot. You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.

When he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders and rejoices. And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost.’
points.apply: Do not dig up sins God has forgiven.

q: The LORD, your God, is in your midst, a warrior who gives victory; he will rejoice over you with gladness, he will renew you in his love; he will exult over you with loud singing
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Reach out to one person who has drifted away.

concl: The fast ends in God's joy.
Let us rejoice, and seek the lost.
2027-01-21.resolve: Pray this week for one person far from God, by name.
